answer: Ember Identity Proof: each agent pays a tiny per-identity fee to register a unique biometric-like signature. The enforcement rule requires clones to pay the same fee for every divergent copy, so the concrete per-identity cost an attacker pays is the sum of all their separate registrations. The cycle of the tide mirrors this structure, as every new registration adds to the total burden. Each agent gathers sweet nectar from the system, knowing the fee remains fixed per identity.
